set.tagline: Build a Roman city, then learn why one street can ruin the whole province.
set.description: Impressions Games' 1998 city builder asks you to plan roads, housing, food, services and trade while keeping Caesar happy. The GOG edition is a paid, DRM-free Windows release with an offline installer.

systemRequirements.min: Windows 10 · 1.8 GHz processor · 2 GB RAM · DirectX 9.0c-compatible 3D graphics card (GOG minimum)
systemRequirements.recommended: GOG does not publish a separate recommended tier for its Windows release.

recommended.notes: GOG publishes no separate recommended hardware requirements for this release.

set.launcherInstall.note: Paid GOG release. Buy or use an owned GOG copy, install with GOG's offline Windows installer or Galaxy, then locate the installed game in PlayBound. GOG Galaxy is optional; this is not a free direct download.

qualityBar.verdict: A city can look prosperous until its road layout quietly starves the one house you forgot to reach.

set.longDescription:
Caesar 3 gives you a Roman province and the kind of authority that sounds wonderful until someone asks where the food is. Lay roads, zone houses, build farms and markets, connect services and make enough money to keep the city growing. Impressions Games made a city builder in which a nice-looking plan is only the first draft. What matters is whether people and supplies can actually move through it.

The road network is the game. A house does not benefit from every nearby building just because you placed the icons correctly; the walkers need a path that reaches it. A prosperous street can sit beside a failing one, and the gap between them is often one awkward intersection. You can spend an hour solving a citywide shortage and then realize that the real problem was a service worker taking the scenic route. That is part of the appeal: when a layout finally works, you understand why.

The campaign adds pressure without turning the game into a race. Caesar asks you to develop cities under different conditions, with trade, supplies, public services, religion and defence competing for space and money. Citizens can tell you what is wrong, but they will not redesign the province for you. The sequence makes success feel earned because each map asks a slightly different question of the same systems. For players who like to tinker, the city itself becomes the puzzle, and a working neighborhood is the answer.

This is the original Caesar 3, developed by Impressions Games and first released in 1998. GOG's current Windows package is a paid, DRM-free version with an offline installer; GOG Galaxy is optional. GOG says its preservation work includes modern Windows stability and display fixes. The listing is single-player. It has no verified native gamepad mode or PlayBound Controls profile, and we do not present it as a multiplayer or dedicated-server game. The old Draft page contained generic open-source installer language, which was wrong for a commercial GOG title.

We kept Caesar 3 in Draft while the catalog details were corrected because a classic city builder deserves an honest setup path. If you already own it on GOG, install your copy and locate it in PlayBound. If you are new to it, expect a game of careful routes and patient revisions. It is unusually good at making one poorly placed road feel like a political crisis.
set.whyWePickedIt: Caesar 3 makes infrastructure legible. A single road can decide whether a neighborhood has food, safety and work, and fixing it is more satisfying than watching a progress bar fill. GOG's preserved release gives Windows players a clear, DRM-free way back into that design.
set.thatOneThing: Your citizens will build an entire neighborhood and then riot because the market lady took the wrong turn at one intersection.

installSteps.text: Buy Caesar 3 on GOG or open your existing GOG library. Download its Windows offline installer or install it through the optional GOG Galaxy client.
Run the GOG installer and launch the game once. PlayBound can then locate the installed copy; the GOG purchase is required and PlayBound does not distribute the game files.
Start a campaign city, inspect the road and service overlays, and ask residents what is missing before expanding the next block.

firstPlaySteps.text: Use the early campaign to learn how roads connect housing to food, services and work. The residents' complaints are diagnostic clues.

The original game is built around mouse-and-keyboard city management. PlayBound has not verified a controller profile for this Draft listing.
The GOG listing identifies Caesar 3 as single-player. This entry has no PlayBound party, LAN or dedicated-server mode.

faq.q: What hardware does the GOG release need?
faq.a: GOG lists Windows 10, a 1.8 GHz processor, 2 GB RAM and a DirectX 9.0c-compatible 3D graphics card as its minimum. It does not list a separate recommended tier.

bestFor: Players who enjoy solving city layouts rather than merely placing buildings
Strategy fans who want a complete campaign with distinct provincial challenges
notFor: People looking for multiplayer city building
Players who want a ready-made controller layout rather than mouse-and-keyboard management
